native_findings.contract: Visible room storage has 17 slots. Incoming ItemUses == -1 first scans for the same item ID and increments the slot QTY word. Otherwise the first empty slot receives ItemID, ItemUses, and QTY=0. Full storage returns -1.
Hidden room storage has 15 slots and uses the same ItemUses==-1 same-ID stack rule before first-empty-slot allocation.
Native room QTY stores extra copies beyond the first: removal decrements QTY while QTY>0; only a zero-QTY final copy clears ItemID/ItemUses/QTY from the slot.
Retained MMUD Explorer source names the matching room arrays RoomItems, RoomItemUses, RoomItemQty, InvisItems, InvisItemUses, and InvisItemQty, corroborating the native offset interpretation.

Death room disposal attempts visible add-item twice, then traverses ten exits in native order N,S,E,W,NE,NW,SE,SW,U,D, skipping RoomType 12 RemoteAction and 8 ChangeMap. A global recursion depth gate permits the origin through depth 5.

Normal movement shifts two 20-entry arrays by 19 dwords and writes the newly entered map/room at index 0. Session initialization zeroes both arrays. Nonstandard relocation bypasses this trail update branch.
Fallback scans 20 movement-trail entries newest-first. Each valid room tries visible insertion, then hidden insertion, returning on first success.

For the 100-slot inventory loop, failure of death-room DFS and movement-trail placement is followed by _dispose_of_item_in_room(room 164, map 1, item, uses). If that also fails, the item is cleared/lost.
For the 50-slot secondary/equipment loop, failure of death-room DFS is followed by movement-trail placement and then loss/logging; there is no map 1 room 164 retry.

preserved_boundary.reason: Complete host logoff/hangup, follower/controlled-NPC, leadership, persistence/delete, and reconnect micro-order remains broader than the now-exact death-floor placement contract.
